prompt: What decides whether a page can be generated statically?

choices.text: Whether the site is a blog or documentation
choices.why: The kind of site is the folklore; a page inside a large app can qualify.

choices.text: Being the same for everybody for a while
choices.why: Right. A page that differs per person never qualifies.

choices.text: Whether it uses JavaScript in the browser
choices.why: A static page can ship and run a whole framework.

choices.text: How many pages the site has in total
choices.why: Size changes the build time, not whether a page can be a file.

prompt: Which cost is a static page's alone, compared with server rendering?

choices.text: A slower first byte
choices.why: The first byte is the time to read a file, faster than a render.

choices.text: Crawlers see an empty page
choices.why: The first response carries the page, as with server rendering.

choices.text: It stays wrong until the next build
choices.why: Yes. It is a photograph of the data at the moment of the build.

choices.text: It cannot be cached by a CDN
choices.why: It is the easiest thing of all to cache: the same bytes for everybody.

prompt: Match each term to what it means in this lesson.

pairs.right: Rendering pages into files at build time
Rendering a static page again while the site runs
Regenerating because something said the data changed

right_distractors: Rendering every page on each request

prompt: Why must `prerender.ts` run on a fresh build, never twice on the same one?

choices.text: Node caches the old files
choices.why: Node reads the files again on every run.

choices.text: The second run finds no empty main to fill
choices.why: Right. The first run overwrote dist/index.html, the shell, with the home page.

choices.text: The script deletes dist/ when it finishes
choices.why: It only writes files into dist/.

choices.text: Vite refuses to serve a folder that was written twice
choices.why: Vite is not involved after the build.

prompt: Why is `vite preview` the wrong server to test the prerendered planner with?

choices.text: It does not serve HTML files
choices.why: It serves them; it just answers unknown addresses with index.html.

choices.text: It compresses everything it sends
choices.why: Compression would not change which page comes back.

choices.text: It answers any unknown address with index.html
choices.why: Yes. A static host answers with the folder's own index.html or a 404.

choices.text: It needs TypeScript
choices.why: It serves built files, whatever they were written in.

prompt: What status did `static.ts` send for `/courses/nonsense`?
How did Nuxt's `generate` and SvelteKit's prerenderer find the three course pages?

choices.text: From generateStaticParams
choices.why: That is Next.js's list.

choices.text: By following the links of the home page
choices.why: Right. Both crawl from /.

choices.text: By reading courses.json at build time, directly
choices.why: That is what prerender.ts and Angular's getPrerenderParams do.

choices.text: From the sitemap
choices.why: The projects have no sitemap.

prompt: A course exists in courses.json but no page links to it. Which projects leave it out of the build, with no error?
hint: Which ones find pages by following links?

choices.text: Next.js and Angular
choices.why: Both list their slugs from the data, so they find it.

choices.text: All four
choices.why: Two of them never look at links.

choices.text: Nuxt and SvelteKit
choices.why: Yes. A crawler only finds what is linked, and the build still succeeds.

choices.text: None: every build fails on a missing page
choices.why: Both kinds fail in silence, which is the warning of the section.

prompt: SvelteKit wrote `courses/git.html`. What can go wrong on a plain static host?

choices.text: Nothing: every host maps an address to a .html file
choices.why: Some only look for git/index.html.

choices.text: The page loses its JavaScript
choices.why: The file name does not change what the page contains.

choices.text: The browser downloads it instead of showing it
choices.why: A .html file is served as a page.

choices.text: Some hosts miss it at `/courses/git`
choices.why: Right. trailingSlash switches SvelteKit to git/index.html.

prompt: You change a title in public/courses.json and do not rebuild. What does static.ts serve for that course?

choices.text: The old title, with a 200
choices.why: Yes. The page is the file the last build wrote.

choices.text: The new title, because static.ts reads from disk
choices.why: It reads dist/ from disk, and dist/ still holds the old page.

choices.text: A 404, because the data and the page disagree
choices.why: Nothing compares them; that is why stale pages go unnoticed.

choices.text: An error from the build
choices.why: No build ran.

prompt: In the timing run, how many seconds did prerender.ts take for 5000 courses?
hint: The last line the loop printed.

prompt: One title changes on a site of a hundred thousand prerendered pages. What does a plain rebuild cost?

choices.text: The time to render the one page that changed
choices.why: A plain build has no idea which page changed.

choices.text: Every page rendered again
choices.why: Right. That is the cost regeneration removes.

choices.text: Nothing, because the files are cached
choices.why: The build rewrites them whatever a cache holds.

choices.text: Only the time to copy the files to the host, with no rendering
choices.why: Copying comes after rendering every page.

prompt: Under regeneration by age, which request is the last to see the old page?

choices.text: The first one after the data changed
choices.why: Requests while the copy is still fresh see it too, and so does one more.

choices.text: None: the page changes the moment the data does
choices.why: Nothing watches the data under regeneration by age.

choices.text: The one that starts the render
choices.why: Yes. Its render is for the person after it.

choices.text: The one that arrives during the render
choices.why: That one may see it too, but the one that started the render is the reliable answer.

prompt: Two Node servers behind a load balancer each run Next.js with regeneration. What happens after the data changes?

choices.text: Both regenerate at the same moment
choices.why: Each regenerates when one of its own requests finds its own copy old.

choices.text: The load balancer regenerates the page
choices.why: A load balancer forwards requests; it renders nothing.

choices.text: Their copies go stale at different times
choices.why: Right. A shared store of copies is what a host built for these frameworks adds.

choices.text: Regeneration stops working
choices.why: It works on each server, separately.

prompt: Serving a copy past its freshness while a fresh one is fetched is called stale-while-___.
hint: The same word Next.js uses for its first number.

prompt: Why does the lesson leave `stale` out of `cacheLife({ revalidate: 10, expire: 3600 })`?

choices.text: Under 30 s it removes the data from the prerender
choices.why: Yes. The build then refuses the page as uncached.

choices.text: Next.js 16 removed the stale field
choices.why: It is still there, defaulting to five minutes.

choices.text: stale only applies to images
choices.why: It is how long the browser's router may reuse a page.

choices.text: It would make the page regenerate every second, whatever revalidate says
choices.why: stale does not decide when the server regenerates.

prompt: Eleven seconds after the data changed, the response said `x-nextjs-cache: STALE` and *Git*. What did Next.js do?

choices.text: Failed to read courses.json
choices.why: Nothing failed; the next request had the new title.

choices.text: Rendered a new page before answering
choices.why: Then the answer would have had the new title.

choices.text: Served it old, rendering behind
choices.why: Right. A second later the new copy was a HIT.

choices.text: Sent the page from the browser's cache
choices.why: curl has no cache; the server sent it.

prompt: Next.js sent `Cache-Control: s-maxage=10, stale-while-revalidate=___` for a page with revalidate 10 and expire 3600.
hint: The hour, minus the ten seconds.

prompt: Why does the revalidation address check a secret?

choices.text: Next.js refuses route handlers without one
choices.why: The check is in the handler's own code.

choices.text: So the page is encrypted
choices.why: The secret encrypts nothing.

choices.text: Anyone could call it in a loop
choices.why: Yes. A server started without a secret refuses everybody.

choices.text: To tell which editor changed the data
choices.why: One shared secret identifies nobody.

prompt: What does `cacheTag("plan")` let one call of `revalidateTag` do?

choices.text: Mark every page rendered from the plan at once
choices.why: Right. The home page and the course pages agree after one call.

choices.text: Rebuild the whole site
choices.why: Nothing is built; marked copies are rendered again when asked for.

choices.text: Mark only the page whose address was called
choices.why: That would be revalidatePath; the tag finds every page that read the data.

choices.text: Delete courses.json
choices.why: It never touches the data, only the copies made from it.

prompt: After the call with the secret, the first request for the Git page still said *Git*. What does the lesson conclude?

choices.text: The call failed
choices.why: It answered revalidated, and the second request had the new title.

choices.text: Test the promise with a request
choices.why: Yes. The documented promise did not hold on this version, and only a request showed it.

choices.text: The secret was wrong
choices.why: A wrong secret is answered with forbidden.

choices.text: expire: 0 only works on a host
choices.why: The lesson makes no such claim; it reports what happened here.

prompt: Nuxt sends no HIT or STALE header. How does the lesson tell which copy came back?

choices.text: By the cache-control header
choices.why: It is the same on every answer.

choices.text: By the last-modified date
choices.why: Right. A new copy carries a new date.

choices.text: By the size of the page
choices.why: The title changes the size by a few bytes, which curl did not print.

choices.text: By asking Nuxt's server log
choices.why: The log was not read; the headers were enough.

prompt: Why does this section use `npm run build` and not `npm run generate`?

choices.text: generate is slower
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: generate cannot read courses.json
choices.why: It read it in the previous section.

choices.text: swr needs a running server
choices.why: Yes. swr regenerates on the server; a folder of files cannot.

choices.text: build is what routeRules requires
choices.why: routeRules also apply to generate; prerender rules are used by it.

prompt: An editor changes product descriptions by pressing Save, and the page may never lag. Which fits?

choices.text: Static generation, rebuilt nightly
choices.why: It can be wrong for a whole day.

choices.text: Regeneration by age, one minute
choices.why: A minute of lag is still lag.

choices.text: On demand, tested
choices.why: Right. Save can make the call, and the previous sections show why the next request must be tested.

choices.text: Client rendering
choices.why: It works, and loses the first-response content the page needs to be found.

prompt: A page shows a feed read from another company's server, which tells nobody when it changes. Which regeneration can keep it current?

choices.text: Only an age
choices.why: Yes. Nothing can call an address when the data changes behind the site's back.

choices.text: Only on demand
choices.why: The other company does not call your address.

choices.text: Either one, with the same result
choices.why: On demand needs someone to make the call.

choices.text: Neither: the page must be rendered in the browser
choices.why: It can be static with an age.

prompt: Put the four answers of the Next.js ISR run in the order they came back.
items: HIT, Git, the file from the build
HIT, Git, just after the data changed
HIT, Git and GitHub, a second after that

prompt: Match each project to where its prerendered course page was written.
Which of these can leave a page out of a static build without any error? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A crawler that finds no link to it
choices.why: Yes, that is how Nuxt and SvelteKit miss a page.

choices.text: A list of slugs that forgot it
choices.why: Yes, the list is all generateStaticParams knows.

choices.text: A course title with an accent in it
choices.why: Text in a title does not change which pages exist.

choices.text: A page that is the same for everybody
choices.why: That is the kind of page a static build is for.
